# 2

For other uses, see [2 (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_(disambiguation)), [II (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/II_(disambiguation)), and [Number Two (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number_Two_(disambiguation)).

| |     |     |     | | --- | --- | --- | | [← 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1) | 2 | [3 →](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3) | | | --- | | [Cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_numeral) | two | | [Ordinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinal_numeral) | 2nd (second) | | [Roman numeral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_numerals) | II, ii | | [Chinese numeral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_numeral) | 二，弍，貳 | | [Devanāgarī](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devan%C4%81gar%C4%AB) | २ | _ _ _ |

**2** ( **two**) is a [number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number), [numeral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numeral_(linguistics)) and [digit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Numerical_digit). It is the [natural number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_number) following [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1) and preceding [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3). It is the smallest and the only even [prime number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_number).

## Mathematics
The number 2 is the second natural number, after [1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1). Each natural number, including 2, is constructed by succession, that is, by adding 1 to the previous natural number.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-1) 2 is the smallest and the only even [prime number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_number), and the first [Ramanujan prime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramanujan_prime). [[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-2) It is also the first [superior highly composite number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_highly_composite_number),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-3) and the first [colossally abundant number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colossally_abundant_number).

[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-6)

[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-9)

In algebra, structures of [characteristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Characteristic_(algebra)) 2 have special behavior because 1+1=0{\displaystyle 1+1=0}![{\displaystyle 1+1=0}](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/8a94a15bb0333c813ac2ed0d697e5e57092cbbc8); in particular, every element satisfies x=−x{\displaystyle x=-x}![{\displaystyle x=-x}](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/5376684ec07dcd4c3163643a126b804231d715fc).

## As a word
_Two_ is most commonly a [determiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_determiners) used with [plural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_number) countable nouns, as in _two days_ or _I'll take these two_. [[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-12) _Two_ is a [noun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_nouns) when it refers to the number two as in _two plus two is four._

The word _two_ is derived from the [Old English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_English) words _twā_ ( [feminine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammatical_gender)), _tū_ (neuter), and _twēġen_ (masculine, which survives today in the form [twain](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/twain)). [[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2#cite_note-OED-13)
